description:
Jansen-Rit model

The Jansen-Rit neural mass model [Jansen1995] has been widely used to simulate physiological signals from various recording methods like intracranial LFPs, and scalp MEG/EEG recordings.

For example, it has been shown to recreate responses similar to evoked-related potentials after a series of impulse stimulations [David2003], [David_etal06], generating high-alpha and low-beta oscillations (with added recurrent inhibitory connections and spike-rate modulation) [Moran2007], and also seizure patterns similar to those seen in temporal lobe epilepsy [Wendling2001]. This biologically motivated model comprises of three main populations of neurons: excitatory pyramidal neurons, inhibitory interneurons, and excitatory interneurons. These populations interact with each other through synaptic connections, forming a feedback loop that produces oscillatory activity governed by a set of nonlinear ordinary differential equations [JansenRit], [David2003], [Kazemi2022].

[Jansen1995]Jansen, B. H., & Rit, V. G. (1995). Electroencephalogram and visual evoked potential generation in a mathematical model of coupled cortical columns. Biological Cybernetics, 73(4), 357-366.
[David2003]David, O., & Friston, K. J. (2003). A neural mass model for MEG/EEG: coupling and neuronal dynamics. NeuroImage, 20(3), 1743-1755. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2003.07.015
[David_etal06]David, O., Kiebel, S. J., Harrison, L. M., Mattout, J., Kilner, J. M., & Friston, K. J. (2006). Dynamic causal modeling of evoked responses in EEG and MEG. NeuroImage, 30(4), 1255-1272. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2005.10.045.
[Moran2007]Moran, R. J., Kiebel, S. J., Stephan, K. E., Reilly, R. B., Daunizeau, J., & Friston, K. J. (2007). A neural mass model of spectral responses in electrophysiology. NeuroImage, 37(3), 706-720. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2007.05.032.
[Wendling2001]Wendling, F., Bartolomei, F., Bellanger, J.-J., & Chauvel, P. (2001). Interpretation of interdependencies in epileptic signals using a macroscopic physiological model of the EEG. Clinical Neurophysiology, 112(7), 1201-1218.
[JansenRit]Jansen, B. H., & Rit, V. G. (1995). Electroencephalogram and visual evoked potential generation in a mathematical model of coupled cortical columns. Biological Cybernetics, 73, 357-366.
[Kazemi2022]Kazemi, S., & Jamali, Y. (2022). On the influence of input triggering on the dynamics of the Jansen-Rit oscillators network. arXiv preprint arXiv:2202.06634.

arguments.G: Scaling the strength of network connections.
arguments.v: Potential at half of maximum firing rate.
arguments.r: Slope of sigmoid function at v:sub:`0`.
arguments.v0: Potential at half of maximum firing rate.
arguments.C0: Average numbers of synapses between EP.
arguments.C1: Average numbers of synapses between EP.
arguments.C2: Average numbers of synapses between IP.
arguments.C3: Average numbers of synapses between IP.
arguments.a: Time constant of excitatory PSP (a = 100 s^-1).
arguments.b: Time constant of inhibitory PSP (b = 50 s^-1).
arguments.decimate: Decimation factor for the output time series.
arguments.dtype: Data type to use for the simulation, `float` for `float64` or `f` for `float32`.
arguments.initial_state: Initial state of the system of shape (`num_nodes`, `num_sim`).
arguments.same_initial_state: If True, all simulations have the same initial state. Default value: False.
arguments.same_noise_per_sim: If True, all simulations have the same noise. Default value: False.
